title: Ministry unveils form to reduce number of forms
summary_es: Sátira original al estilo de un diario británico: un ministerio presenta un formulario de catorce páginas para solicitar rellenar menos formularios.
prediction_prompt: How does a satirical news story make you laugh without ever telling a joke? Think about tone.

sentences.text: The Department for Administrative Simplification yesterday announced what it described as "a decisive step towards a leaner state": a new form, running to fourteen pages, on which members of the public may apply to complete fewer forms.
The document, officially designated SF-1 but already known in Whitehall as "the form to end all forms", will be available from next month at post offices, libraries and, in due course, online.
Applicants are advised that a separate form, SF-1a, must first be submitted in order to request it.

Launching the initiative before an audience of journalists and what appeared to be several civil servants who had wandered in by mistake, the minister responsible, Sir Gerald Penhallow, was in buoyant mood.
"For too long," he declared, "the citizens of this country have been drowning in paperwork. Today we throw them a lifeline."

The lifeline, he went on to explain, would itself require a signature in three places, proof of address and a countersignature from a person of good standing who had known the applicant for at least two years and was not a relative, a neighbour or, for reasons he did not elaborate upon, a dentist.
Sir Gerald was at pains to stress that the scheme had been designed with simplicity in mind.
Sections one to nine, he noted, need only be completed by those applicants to whom they apply, a category the guidance notes define as "most people".
Section ten, which asks respondents to list every form they have filled in since 1987, is described as optional, although leaving it blank invalidates the application.
Asked whether this might not deter the very people the form was intended to help, the minister replied that he rejected the premise of the question, and then, after a pause, the question.

The department's own impact assessment, a document of some two hundred pages, concludes that the measure will reduce the administrative burden on the average household by "up to eleven minutes a year", once the six hours required to complete SF-1 have been, in its phrase, "amortised over a lifetime".
It concedes that the saving may be smaller for applicants who die.
The digital version of the form has attracted particular praise from the department itself.

"Users will be able to save their progress at any time," a press release explains, "and return to it within twenty minutes, after which, for reasons of security, the session will expire and all information will be lost."

The online portal will be compatible with most browsers released before 2014 and will be closed for maintenance at weekends, on public holidays and between the hours of six in the evening and nine the following morning, "in line with user demand".

Those who encounter problems are invited to telephone a helpline, where a recorded voice will inform them that the department is experiencing a higher volume of calls than usual, as it has done continuously since the helpline opened.
Reaction was mixed.

A spokesman for the Federation of Small Businesses welcomed the announcement "in principle", adding that his members would study the details as soon as they had finished the forty-page consultation questionnaire on whether they had time to study the details.
The opposition accused the government of "tinkering at the edges", and promised that, if elected, it would establish a commission to consider the case for a review.
Not everyone was so restrained.

Outside the ministry, a small demonstration had gathered under a banner reading "DOWN WITH THIS SORT OF THING", though it later emerged that most of those present had come to protest about something else and had been unable to find the right building.
One protester, a retired surveyor from Leatherhead who gave his name only as "the undersigned", said he had been trying to cancel a television licence since the spring of 2011.
"I have filled in everything they have sent me," he said. "Last month they sent me a form asking how satisfied I was with the forms. I gave it four out of five. I didn't want any trouble."
Academic opinion is divided.
Professor Helena Marsh, who has studied public administration for thirty years and describes the experience as "instructive", believes the form may represent a genuine turning point.
"Until now," she said, "bureaucracy has grown more or less by accident. This is the first time I have seen it reproduce deliberately."
She added that she had been asked to evaluate the scheme and had agreed to do so as soon as her application to evaluate it had been approved.
Officials privately admit that the project has not been without its difficulties.

An earlier pilot, conducted in a market town in the Midlands, was abandoned after the forms intended to measure its success were sent to the wrong town, where residents nevertheless completed them, reporting high levels of satisfaction with a scheme of which they had no experience.
The results were subsequently hailed as encouraging.
There are those, of course, who will say that all this is absurd; that a state which answers every difficulty with a document has mistaken the map for the territory.
To them the department has a ready answer, set out in paragraph 4.2 of the guidance notes: complaints about SF-1 should be made in writing, on form SF-2.
SF-2 is expected to be available in the autumn.
It is understood to be quite long.
A shorter version is under consideration, subject to the outcome of a form.

language_focus.title_es: El humor está en el tono, no en los chistes
language_focus.explanation_es: El texto nunca se ríe: usa el registro impasible de un diario serio (*It concedes that…*, *It is understood to be…*, pasivas, fuentes anónimas) para contar disparates. Cuanto más sobria es la frase, más absurdo resulta lo que dice: *The results were subsequently hailed as encouraging*.

language_focus.title_es: El remate al final de la frase
language_focus.explanation_es: Muchas frases guardan el giro para la última palabra: *…or, for reasons he did not elaborate upon, a dentist*; *…the premise of the question, and then, after a pause, the question*. Los incisos entre comas retrasan el final a propósito, para que caiga con más fuerza.

glossary.def_en: using only what is necessary, with nothing wasted
at some time in the future, when the time is right (often vague in official language)
a person who works for a government department
a rope thrown to rescue someone in the water; something that saves you from a difficult situation
respected and with a good reputation (a formula found on official documents)
glossary.def_es: de reconocida solvencia, de buena reputación

glossary.def_en: to make a special effort to do something
glossary.def_es: esforzarse por, poner mucho empeño en

glossary.def_en: an idea that an argument or a question is based on
to spread a cost over a long period
to make small changes that do not deal with the real problem
glossary.def_es: hacer retoques sin entrar en el fondo

glossary.def_en: in formal letters, the person who has signed below
to describe something publicly as very good
a system of official rules and paperwork, especially when it seems too complicated

tasks.prompt: What kind of text is this?

options.text: A genuine press release issued by a government department
A satirical piece written in the style of a news report
An opinion column calling for the civil service to be abolished
A historical account of a failed reform

tasks.rationale_es: Tiene la forma de una noticia (fuentes, citas, datos), pero lo que cuenta es deliberadamente absurdo: un formulario para pedir menos formularios, que a su vez exige otro formulario.

tasks.prompt: What is the main target of the writer's humour?

options.text: Citizens who refuse to cooperate with the authorities
Journalists who misreport what the government has decided to do
The high cost of putting public services online
Officialdom that grows while claiming to shrink

tasks.rationale_es: Todo el texto gira en torno a una administración que responde al exceso de papeleo con más papeleo; la profesora lo resume: es la primera vez que ve a la burocracia «reproducirse a propósito».

tasks.prompt: What is the effect of the last sentence of paragraph 1?

options.text: It quietly shows that the scheme adds to the problem
It reassures readers that the new process will be straightforward
It explains why the form cannot yet be found online
It criticises applicants for being careless

tasks.rationale_es: Para pedir el formulario que reduce formularios hay que rellenar antes otro: la frase, dicha sin énfasis, desmonta el anuncio.

tasks.prompt: What does the detail about the dentist (paragraph 2) suggest?

options.text: Dentists are widely known to be unreliable witnesses
The minister has a personal dislike of the medical profession
Official rules can be arbitrary and go unexplained
Applicants will need a certificate of good health

tasks.rationale_es: La exclusión del dentista no tiene lógica y el ministro no la explica (*for reasons he did not elaborate upon*): parodia las condiciones caprichosas de los formularios.

tasks.prompt: "Sir Gerald was at pains to stress…" (paragraph 3) means that he

options.text: made a special effort to emphasise it
found it uncomfortable to admit in front of journalists
refused to confirm it
was unwell while explaining it

tasks.rationale_es: *Be at pains to do something* = poner mucho empeño en hacerlo. No tiene nada que ver con dolor físico.

tasks.prompt: Applicants may leave section ten blank without any consequences.
tasks.rationale_es: Se describe como *optional*, pero dejarla en blanco *invalidates the application*: opcional solo de nombre.

tasks.prompt: What is implied by the phrase "amortised over a lifetime" in paragraph 4?

options.text: The form has to be completed again every year
Older applicants will be dealt with before younger ones
The department expects most applicants to give up halfway
The saving only exceeds the effort across several decades

tasks.rationale_es: Seis horas para ahorrar once minutos al año solo compensan repartidas en toda una vida; de ahí el remate de que el ahorro será menor para quien muera antes.

tasks.prompt: How is the opposition presented in paragraph 6?

options.text: As having a clear and detailed alternative plan of its own
As no more decisive than those it criticises
As secretly in favour of the scheme
As uninterested in the issue

tasks.rationale_es: Acusa al gobierno de hacer retoques y promete… una comisión que estudie la conveniencia de una revisión: tres pasos sin hacer nada.

tasks.prompt: Why did the protester rate the forms "four out of five"?

options.text: He was, on the whole, fairly pleased with the service he had received
He had misread the scale
He feared that honesty would bring more paperwork
He hoped to be offered compensation

tasks.rationale_es: *I didn't want any trouble*: lleva desde 2011 atrapado en trámites y no se atreve a quejarse por si le llega otro formulario.

tasks.prompt: What is ironic about the pilot scheme described in paragraph 9?

options.text: It was praised on the word of people it never reached
It cost a great deal more than the national scheme will
Its results were kept from the public
Local residents refused to take part

tasks.rationale_es: Los cuestionarios llegaron a otro pueblo, cuyos vecinos se declararon muy satisfechos con algo que no conocían, y aun así los resultados se celebraron como alentadores.

tasks.prompt: Online users can save their work and come back to it the next day.
tasks.rationale_es: Solo pueden volver *within twenty minutes*; después la sesión caduca y se pierde todo.

tasks.prompt: Sir Gerald has previously been a minister in another department.
tasks.rationale_es: El texto solo lo presenta como el ministro responsable; no dice nada de su trayectoria.

tasks.prompt: Which best describes how the humour of the piece works?

options.text: The writer openly insults the minister
Emotional, exaggerated language is used from beginning to end
Readers are addressed directly and urged to protest
Absurd events are related in a sober, official tone

tasks.rationale_es: El narrador nunca opina ni exagera: cuenta disparates con la frialdad de una noticia (*It concedes that…*, *It is understood to be quite long*). El contraste entre tono y contenido es lo que hace reír.

tasks.prompt: Complete the sentence with one word from the final paragraph in each gap.
tasks.text: Critics say that a state which answers every difficulty with a document "has mistaken the {{1}} for the {{2}}".
tasks.rationale_es: *To mistake the map for the territory*: confundir la representación (el documento) con la realidad que representa.
